issues.what: the rise cover ends on a flat, band-free beige disk. The bands, small detail and star field then pop in within two frames, and the color jumps from grey-beige to bright cream by 3280 (sheet-05)
issues.fix: hold the banded albedo texture and the stars at low contrast through the whole blur, and cross-fade detail and color over 8-12 frames instead of 2

issues.what: the limb goes from a shallow slope rising to the right to a steep arc in one frame. That reads as a snap in camera roll or direction, not one continuous move
issues.fix: spread the roll/yaw change over the cover with an eased curve so the limb angle rotates step by step

issues.what: the stars and Milky Way drop to pure black during the dive cover, then come back at 3026-3030. The exposure and sky do not carry across the cover. The same happens at 3267-3274 in sheet-06
issues.fix: keep the star field rendered (motion-blurred) through the cover, or dim it gradually, instead of cutting it to black

issues.what: Jupiter grows from about half the frame to filling it in 8 frames, after a nearly static hold. The dive start feels like a lurch, not an eased acceleration. The matching end of the rise, 3274-3287 in sheet-05, is just as abrupt
issues.fix: ease into the dive with a longer acceleration ramp, and ease the pull-back of the rise to a stop the same way

issues.what: the orange storm streaks smear into parallel, repeated vertical strands that look like ghost copies more than one smooth blur
issues.fix: raise the motion-blur sample count or shutter samples during the fast segments

issues.what: the bright cloud fragments show stepped, duplicated edges in the blur
issues.fix: use more temporal samples for the motion blur in the first frames of the cover

issues.what: the vortex mostly grows and tilts as one sheet. The near cloud tops show little parallax against the horizon, so depth reads weakly
issues.fix: add a small lateral or forward camera move so the foreground cloud relief slides against the limb
